sets.title: Bounded lexer with exact progress

objective_text.T60.01.a: Derive and defend: Derive the pre-multiply bound and exact consumed extent, including an unterminated span. Explain why end-of-input is a successful token distinct from rejection.
objective_text.T60.01.b: Implement and investigate: Implement cc_token over a nonterminated byte span. Skip ASCII space/newline/tab; recognize decimal0..65535(kind1), x(2), ((3), )(4), +(5), *(6), and end(0). Return1 on token/end,0 on invalid or overflow. On failure preserve offset/kind/value. On success set value0 except constants. Do not call strtol or a lexer library.

Then Add hexadecimal constants and comments; distinguish preprocessing tokens from semantic tokens and preserve exact diagnostic spans without accepting partial malformed literals.

sets.title: Precedence parser and bounded syntax construction

objective_text.T60.02.a: Derive and defend: Prove each parser level consumes its grammar production or rejects, and derive linear token work with bounded recursion. Explain why no partially constructed IR is publishable.
objective_text.T60.02.b: Implement and investigate: Implement cc_parse from the declared expression grammar, generating postfix CONST/ARG/ADD/MUL followed by RET. Multiplication binds tighter than addition; parentheses override. Limit nesting to16 and IR capacity to caller storage. On failure used remains unchanged; partially written IR scratch is unspecified and must never be executed. Reject every unconsumed nonspace byte.
objective_text.T60.02.c: Falsify and transfer: A parser accepts the valid prefix2 of2? and silently drops the error. Another implements2+3*x as(2+3)*x. Separate tokenization, grouping and lowering defects. Then Add subtraction and left associativity, then introduce a side-effecting call and state which source sequencing must be preserved rather than inferred from precedence.

sets.title: Subset type and arithmetic semantics

objective_text.T60.03.a: Derive and defend: Derive modulo behavior independently of host signed overflow; identify absent signed conversions, floating-point rules and pointer semantics rather than pretending they are covered.
objective_text.T60.03.b: Implement and investigate: Implement cc_binary(op,a,b,out) for op3 addition and4 multiplication modulo2^32, using uint64_t intermediates and explicit conversion. Reject other opcodes without changing output. Identify the host assumptions required by uint32_t/uint64_t and compare with the C unsigned-return wrapper.
objective_text.T60.03.c: Falsify and transfer: A backend replaces multiplication by addition or performs signed overflow in its evaluator. Passing small positive constants is insufficient evidence. Then Add a signed32 type with explicit overflow diagnostics, usual arithmetic conversions and casts; construct a case where the unsigned and signed programs must differ.

sets.title: Typed intermediate representation and interpreter

objective_text.T60.04.a: Derive and defend: Associate every opcode with input/output type and stack effect; prove validated execution cannot underflow/overflow its bounded stack and returns the expression denotation.
objective_text.T60.04.b: Implement and investigate: Implement cc_run over verified CCIns with a local64-entry uint32_t stack and one x argument. CONST and ARG push; ADD/MUL consume two and push one; RET must be last with exactly one value. Reject malformed streams and preserve output. Use cc_binary for semantic arithmetic, not native signed expressions.
objective_text.T60.04.c: Falsify and transfer: A nominal interpreter reports success without publishing the computed result, while another executes malformed IR before checking its stack effects. Then Add basic blocks and conditional branches; derive join-state type/stack compatibility and bound or explicitly budget loops before extending execution.

sets.title: IR verification and resource bounds

objective_text.T60.05.a: Derive and defend: Derive prefix-height and terminal-height conditions and peak stack bytes separately for the two backends. Explain the verifier assumptions that remain outside its scope.
objective_text.T60.05.b: Implement and investigate: Implement cc_validate for1..128 instructions, at most64 live stack values, constants<=65535, opcodes1..5, no underflow, and exactly one final RET with height1. Return peak depth only on success. Reject any operation after RET and any missing RET.
objective_text.T60.05.c: Falsify and transfer: The faulty verifier accepts executable instructions after RET. Then Serialize IR to a bytecode file; add version, checked count arithmetic and canonical endianness, then fuzz parser and verifier independently.

sets.title: Original x86-64 code emission

objective_text.T60.06.a: Derive and defend: Map each IR stack transition to emitted instructions, prove balanced machine stack and identify all clobbered registers. The textual anchor is weaker than assembling and executing the result.
objective_text.T60.06.b: Implement and investigate: Implement cc_x86 emitting NUL-terminated GNU assembly for cm_expr(unsigned x) from valid IR using edi input, eax result, rcx temporary and64-bit push/pop storage. Use bounded staging so too-small output capacity leaves caller bytes unchanged. No LLVM, compiler library or template compiler may replace emission.
objective_text.T60.06.c: Falsify and transfer: The mutant lowers multiply as addition. A different faulty emitter uses64-bit multiply without the required unsigned32 truncation. Differential execution must expose the semantic mismatch. Then Add an actual function call: preserve argument x across it, restore16-byte call alignment and compare caller-saved/callee-saved decisions under nested expressions.

sets.title: Original Thumb code emission

objective_text.T60.07.a: Derive and defend: Prove the private operand stack remains word-aligned and returns to its public8-byte boundary. Identify the Thumb-state return and why r3 would not survive a newly added call.
objective_text.T60.07.b: Implement and investigate: Implement cc_thumb emitting Thumb-2 GNU assembly using r3 to retain x, r0/r1 temporaries, word pushes/pops and bx lr. Constants fit movw. No nested calls or FP operations are supported. Stage output transactionally and preserve the exact same unsigned32 semantics as x86.
objective_text.T60.07.c: Falsify and transfer: The backend omits argument preservation, so expressions that load x after a constant compute from the constant instead. A constant-only test cannot detect this. Then Retarget Thumb-1 without movw or the same instruction set assumptions; synthesize constants, inspect helper dependencies and execute on the corresponding emulator CPU.
